turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: What brings you in today?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I've just been feeling like very nauseated for, it feels like all the time right now.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: When did this start?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's been over a week. Maybe not quite two weeks, but like around then. Yeah, maybe like 9 days.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And um, is it, do you always have the sensation of nausea or is it related, or does it come and go?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Oh, I think it's like worse when I am smelling something really bad, and it's worse in the morning. But I feel like it's always kind of there.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: I see OK. Um, have you had any vomiting?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, yeah, like um, yeah, like a lot of days I'll throw up like once or twice.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And this has all been over the past week, week two weeks or so?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, um, any other symptoms that you have?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Oh no, just, well, like I feel like I've I've had to pee a lot more. Um, but I don't, I don't think that's like related. I think maybe I have just been drinking a lot of water, so yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: How often do you have to pee?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Oh, like, I feel like every couple hours right now.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, so say every two hours, every hour, every five hours?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Probably every probably every like 2, maybe, maybe every hour I get certain times in a day.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Do you wake up at night to pee?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Oh, like it doesn't wake me up but it's like I wake up because I hear something. Then I'll be like, oh I think I should probably go to the bathroom.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, do you feel like you have control over when you are going to bathroom or is it difficult for you to hold it in?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Oh I I I can control it. It's just like uncomfortable right?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: I see I see so, um, you have urinary frequency, but do you do you feel like, uh so you said that you can control it, you don't you don't feel like you need to run to the bathroom or you'll pee in your pants?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I don't feel like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Do you have any pain when you're peeing?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: No, OK alright um, do you feel like you've been more thirsty recently? Why do you feel you've been drinking more more water?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I think, I think just 'cause like I was getting I was like throwing up like so like I feel like I was a little dehydrated.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Um, I see OK, um, have you, other than the nausea and vomiting, have you had any other stomach related issues? Any belly pain or changes in your bowel movements?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Ah no, I don't think so, well my stomach has been like it feels like a little crampy. I thought that maybe it could be my period but like I'm not on my period.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: When did you last have your period?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Oh well, let me think. Um, like six weeks ago. I guess that would be, I don't know. I don't really like keep track.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, OK. Do you know if you get your periods regularly or are your periods irregular?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I think they're I think they're usually pretty regular, but I don't I don't like I don't calculate it like to the day.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: True yeah, is it is it normal for you to go six weeks without a period?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Oh, come to think of it, I don't, I don't think so.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright. Um, OK. Uh, have you, I'll just ask you a couple more questions about your symptoms. So I know that you've been nauseous and have vomited a couple of times in the past two weeks. And, you have had some cramps in your belly. Have you had any flu like symptoms?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Nothing like that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I don't think so.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Any headaches?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Any fevers?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Muscle aches?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, um, have you, have you had a cough at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Oh no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and have you noticed any blood in your stools?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Have you, you haven't had any palpitations or chest pain or anything of that sort?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright um can you tell me about your past medical history, any medical issues medical conditions that you have?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, nothing, nothing really.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Have you, um, been taking any medications?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I mean, I've been taking like like I've been chewing like those ginger things that are supposed to help with nausea, but they weren't really helpful.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: I see. Any allergies?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: So just like nickel, like in jewelry, if I wear not real jewellery, it'll give me a rash, but it's not food or like or medications or anything.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Um, and, uh, a couple of questions about your social history. Who do you currently live with?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, like I I just I live with one roommate.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Um and, do you currently smoke?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, you don't smoke, OK. Have you, do you consume alcohol?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no, very rarely because I always get a headache.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, when was the last drink that you had?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Oh gosh, like like a month ago probably.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, um, and you consume any illicit drugs?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, are you currently sexually active?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah just like with my boyfriend.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And do you use protection while having sex?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, we we just use condoms. I used to be on birth control but it always made me feel like like kind of sick so I don't use that anymore.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Mhm, I see, OK. Uh and um, let's see. Family history. Do you do you have any medical conditions that run in your family?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, like I don't, I don't think so. I guess my dad my dad has like high blood pressure, yeah, I don't think there's anything else.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, alright, well, thank you so much for spending time with me today. I think I have gathered all the information that I would have liked. I will go talk to my attending, we'll come back and maybe ask a couple more questions and then share the plan with you.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: OK, thank you.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: You're welcome.
